knoot.headline: A dashboard design that lifted feature adoption by 37%UI/UX Design
knoot.lead: UI/UX design for a personal finance app
knoot.about: Knoot is a personal finance app that helps users track spending across multiple cards. The client asked RZQ to design a premium dashboard with understandable and accessible weekly and monthly spending visibility. It must be effective for people managing several cards and high transaction volume.
knoot.problem: During a competitor audit, we found that on the home screens, users had to scroll through 6–8 tabs before they could see their balance. Making a money transfer also required 6–8 taps. Reviews in app stores and our own testing showed that users got lost in the navigation and described the experience as too complicated due to an excessive amount of information. These obstacles led to task abandonment and negatively impacted user retention.
knoot.solution: UI/UX designers created a focused Analytics dashboard with four key metric cards, a Spending Over Time chart, a customizable Cards screen, and a 3-step onboarding flow with QR code and biometric verification. We rejected denser layouts after testing showed they caused scanning fatigue. In the final design, users see the most-checked metrics first. Our design solutions cut cognitive load and support return visits.

sections.title: Wireframing
sections.text: Our guiding principle was “decision-critical data first, with supporting details available on demand” to reduce the cognitive load from the high volume of transactions across various cards. In an early version of the analytical mockup, the home screen featured six cards with metrics and two charts. But low-fidelity testing revealed that users were overlooking or misinterpreting lower-priority cards. Therefore, we narrowed the list down to four key metrics. Our designers created 28 screen sketches and user flows before beginning work on the high-fidelity design, allowing us to validate the information architecture.

sections.title: Sign up screen
sections.text: The registration screen guides users through three steps, where the primary method of data entry is a QR code scanner, with manual code entry serving as a fallback option. We displayed only a few options at each step to avoid overwhelming new users. Our team moved the advanced security settings from this screen to the process that takes place after registration is complete, as testing showed that their presence increased the number of drop-offs. Contrast ratios across the entire screen meet WCAG AA requirements, and the large font sizes and touch elements are designed for one-handed use on a mobile device.

sections.title: Complex product, confused users? RZQ simplifies the architecture without cutting functionality.
Analytics dashboard
sections.text: The analytics screen shows 4 equally weighted metric cards for an instant financial overview. A wide "Spending Over Time" area chart visualizes trends across months. Early designs planned two additional charts and several secondary metrics on this view, but testing revealed users ignored them once density got too high. So, we moved them behind filters and drill-downs. This tradeoff improved scan speed and made the main view easier to act on.

sections.title: Cards Preview
sections.text: The cards screen displays a large card preview that updates in real time as users change the background, zoom level, rotation, and font using sliders and color swatches. The preview includes tabs for “General,” “Appearance,” “Locked,” and “Accessibility” settings. In earlier versions, this screen also displayed controls for layers and filters. However, testing showed that having too many options at once caused “choice paralysis,” so we moved them to a separate menu. Users still have full customization options; they just don’t see all of them at once.

results.title: Task Completion Rate
results.text: Participants completed the main tasks during the testing session thanks to the four-card control panel and the elimination of deep submenus, which had previously led to high abandonment.

results.title: Design duration
results.text: Validating the information architecture across 28 wireframed screens before high-fidelity design enabled the team to resolve the structure early and avoid rework later.

results.title: Task Efficiency
results.text: Flat navigation, providing one-tap access to the “Transfers,” “Cards,” “Analytics,” and “Settings” sections from the control panel, made the most common tasks easily accessible.

results.title: Feature Adoption Rate
results.text: Intelligent sequencing, placing key metrics, the spending chart, top merchants, and budget breakdown in that order, put the most-used insights where users saw them first.

kinves.headline: Mobile Finance App for Daily Money Management
kinves.about: Kinves is a personal finance app centered on a single home screen, giving users immediate access to their balance and a direct path to everyday money tasks. The client wanted a product people could understand from the first interaction, with routine financial tasks simple enough to complete without a learning curve.
kinves.problem: When a user opens a financial app to look at a single number or do a single action, they have to process several metrics. Secondary data hides balance checks and transfers, making product adoption more difficult, leading to navigational mistakes and less reasons for users to come back.
kinves.solution: Instead of using a single screen to display all of the metrics, we assigned each one an individual priority. The balance now answers the first question at a glance, and a shorter payment flow lets users act faster, creating a 31% decrease in navigation errors and 92% success in transfer task.
kinves.processIntro: We started by researching how other financial apps organize data-heavy dashboards. The results helped our UX team figure out how to define navigation before they looked at visual direction.

sections.text: Before adding supporting content, wireframes assigned each screen a primary purpose. People who use a financial product should never have to stop to figure out which number is important or where the next step starts. That principle was the foundation of every layout.

tunnelo.headline: Branding for a cybersecurity VPN product
tunnelo.about: Tunnelo is a VPN service that gives users secure internet access through a one-tap connection and shows protection status in real time. The team asked RZQ to create a distinctive identity that separates the product from generic tools.
tunnelo.problem: There isn't much space for new brands to stand out in the VPN industry. Tunnelo required a strong visual system that could unify the product, social media, and marketing materials while giving users a distinct and instantly recognizable identity.
tunnelo.solution: Our team used a pixel-inspired font, neon-green accents, and a hexagonal logo to create the brand. Tunnelo maintains its own technical style across all platforms by consistently using the same visual cues in product displays and campaign graphics.
tunnelo.processIntro: Starting from the research phase and continuing to the launch of the product, the project moved through four stages. Each phase was built upon the success of the previous one and helped us create a strong brand that could be used in marketing and digital products.

sections.title: Moodboard
sections.text: Using recognizable visual clichés as a starting point, the moodboard analyzed how cybersecurity could appear more contemporary. It was the combination of pixel visuals, dark tones, and bright green accents that made Tunnelo stand out.

sections.title: Logo Design
sections.text: We created a custom logo using the shape of a tunnel and a digital connection. Pixel-style typography adds character and gives Tunnelo a consistent look in product interfaces and branded materials.

sections.title: Brand Guidelines
sections.text: Our design team transformed the brand into useful, everyday instructions. To ensure that all of Tunnelo's product interfaces and marketing materials have the same consistent aesthetic, the document lays out strict guidelines for the logo and visual layouts.

sections.title: Give your product a distinctive identity users recognize and remember
Social Media

sections.text: To ensure consistency across all physical channels, we modified the brand system for use in posters, outdoor ads, and merchandise. Every piece is easily readable thanks to its large headlines and simple layouts, and it makes a clear connection to Tunnelo in public spaces.

solnex.headline: Digital Platform & Brand Design for Crypto Finance
solnex.lead: One system for crypto, fiat, and daily spending
solnex.about: Solnex is a crypto-first platform that integrates digital assets with everyday balances in a single portfolio. Hidden fees and trader-led interfaces had already made people less trusting of the market the client was going into. RZQ designed the brand, website, app, and (out-of-home advertising) OOH system to make each amount visible early and keep the full asset picture within one flow.
solnex.problem: It became more difficult to trust simple transactions because of hidden fees, market-first home displays, and separate fiat and cryptocurrency balances. This could lengthen the learning curve for a new product and discourage consumers from returning after the first session.
solnex.solution: We made financial visibility the product’s core logic. The users see all of their assets on the home screen when they first log in, and trade costs show up before approval. As a result, users are more likely to complete their first transaction and to return for future practical reasons.
solnex.processIntro: Discovering category hazards established the no-dark-patterns guideline. Branding set the visual system, then the website set the messaging hierarchy, which the app eventually adopted.

sections.title: Wireframing
sections.text: The designers at RZQ began by creating grayscale wireframes to test the page's structural integrity. Resolving concerns prior to enrollment ensured that each claim organically led into proof. So that visual impact wouldn't make up for poor logic, the team didn't use the black-and-magenta style until after that.

sections.title: Logo Design
sections.text: Our design team worked to craft an S-mark that, even at 24 pixels, retains its shape and is easily readable on a billboard. With one scalable form, there was no need for different logos, so the brand's identity stayed the same at launch.

sections.title: Landing Page Layouts
sections.text: Before asking users to sign up, Solnex had to demonstrate the product's functionality. So, the landing page starts with account statuses and numbers, allowing users to evaluate the platform by looking at the product. Even during onboarding, the consistent visual logic serves to minimize relearning and increase the number of users who are able to accomplish the first meaningful activity.

sections.title: Your fintech idea may be complex. Its brand and UX should feel simple .
Mobile App
sections.text: With the app's logic built into the product, users won't have to relearn anything once they've signed up. With a single dashboard that consolidates both daily balances and cryptocurrency, users can get to the important steps faster and come back with a clear goal in mind.

sections.title: Printing Materials
sections.text: We considered out-of-home as an acquisition channel with a three-second dwell time. One message was used to explain Solnex's worth, and the QR code was left as the only next step. Because of it, people were able to grasp the product in a flash, remember the brand better, and go straight from offline reach to app installs.

results.text: The unified dashboard helped users understand their total balance twice as quickly by combining everyday money with crypto.

results.text: People were able to recognize and remember Solnex after just one short exposure thanks to the geometric S-mark and focused visual system.

results.title: First-Transaction Completion
results.text: The shorter flow helped more users complete their first crypto action without backtracking or leaving the process.

fundediq.headline: Brand Identity and UI/UX Design for a prop trading platform
fundediq.lead: One visual system across product, landing, social media, and print

Our team had to balance technological precision with approachability and communicate sophistication, trust, and analytical depth. Branding and UI/UX solutions had to reflect FundedIQ's values: clarity, discipline, and fairness.
fundediq.solution: Clarity drives trust. RZQ delivered branding, graphic design, and UI/UX. We created a dark-toned visual system using glassmorphism and precise accents that carry through to the product. Structured grids and a clear hierarchy allow traders to focus on assessments and progress without confusion or complexity.

sections.text: Brand guidelines protect the identity from inconsistent execution. The document covers logo placement, color palette, typography hierarchy, and spacing standards. Internal teams and external partners now have a clear framework to maintain visual coherence as FundedIQ scales. This stage is important for every project, so we always include the brand guidelines in our design process.

sections.title: UI Layouts
sections.text: Our UI/UX team delivered a complete web layout system with a landing page, product pages, challenge selection, FAQ, 404, and mobile-responsive views. The dark interface uses purple accent colors and structured content blocks to focus and guide traders step by step. Each page balances information density with visual breathing room.

sections.title: RZQ helps trading platforms look as precise as the logic behind them.
Social Media

piko-health.headline: UX and Branding for a Personalized Health and Longevity Platform
piko-health.about: Piko is a personalized digital health platform that combines advanced blood testing, medical programs, and coaching. It helps users optimize biomarkers, manage weight, and slow biological aging. The client partnered with us to design the the brand identity, landing page, and web app.
piko-health.problem: The design shouldn’t be too close to traditional healthcare. Our task was to make the platform feel medically credible but energetic, modern, ambitious, and human. Complex health data had to be understandable without heavy dashboards or distracting interactions. The interface must be simple.
piko-health.solution: A visual identity positions Piko as a performance-focused health platform. To avoid clinical patterns, it uses lifestyle photography, effective typography, and a simple interface. Instead of complex displays, we implemented simple indicators to make biomarker data easier to grasp.
piko-health.processIntro: Our approach was strategic and business-oriented. We looked beyond the interface to understand Piko’s market position, competitive landscape, and long-term growth goals to provide future-relevant design.

sections.title: Logo Concept Design
sections.text: The logo expresses human vitality and avoids common medical symbols . The radial form suggests progress and biological optimization. Its symmetry reflects precision and trust. The bold orange gradient adds energy and helps Piko stand apart from clinical-looking health brands.

sections.title: Clutch Review
sections.text: Everything described in this case study reflects our approach, structure, and design solutions. But the most accurate assessment of our work comes from our clients. Receiving a 5-star rating confirms that our strategic thinking, product experience, and over 10 years of practice translate into true partnership value.

sections.title: Landing Page Layouts
sections.text: The landing page should encourage users to move from inspiration to action through a structured flow. Our UI/UX experts offered a result-oriented hero section with visible signs of trust (research, reviews, compliance) and simplified health information. Each block supports the same goal: to quickly gain trust, demonstrate measurable value, and naturally encourage users to start testing or sign up.

sections.title: When advanced features slow down conversions, it’s time to rethink structure.
Mobile Version

That's why the primary goal at this stage was to eliminate the barrier between curiosity and action on smaller screens. We prioritized thumb-friendly navigation, an intuitive vertical hierarchy, and high-contrast health indicators. Our expert additionally improved the "Start My Test" flow for faster decisions and higher conversions.

sections.title: Web Application Design
sections.text: Our guiding approach for apps is to present users with what is important first, then details. In the Piko app, the overview page displays the Biological Age and Health Score first. We arranged deeper biomarker data, physician notes, and protocols into digestible modules. The AI assistant and progress charts help users comprehend their results and what they should do next.

imed.headline: Pitch Deck Design for a National E-Health Ecosystem
imed.lead: Data-dense content organized into layered storytelling
imed.about: iMed is a national-level e-health ecosystem that centralizes healthcare data and improves medical and administrative workflows for public-sector organizations. RZQ created a pitch deck to effectively communicate this complex system to decision-makers.
imed.problem: The e-health ecosystem had already been established, but communication was challenging. Our team had to structure complicated technical content, including system logic and interoperability layers, into a persuasive visual story that non-technical stakeholders could follow without missing important aspects.
imed.solution: We built a modular slide system with consistent layout patterns to replace text-heavy explanations with charts, maps, and system diagrams. A typographic hierarchy and restrained color system guide attention from the general system overview to specific components and data points.

sections.title: Style
sections.text: RZQ designer created a visual system around four element types. 1. Minimal UI icons for system actions like collect, analyze, and use. 2. Data visualization components, including line charts, bar charts, and percentage blocks. 3. Map-based visuals that communicate national coverage and scale. 4. Structured content cards for repeating information blocks. Every element adheres to the same grid logic, so even data-heavy slides such as national standards or interoperability breakdowns remain scannable.

sections.title: Stakeholders don't have time to decode your product. RZQ makes sure they don't have to.
Pitch Deck
sections.text: The main task was to make an existing system understandable. We used layered storytelling to reorganize content from high-level system value down to specific components like health records, decision support, and analytics. Every slide works as a communication tool that helps stakeholders see how the system operates and why it matters.

sections.title: Printing materials
sections.text: In addition to the pitch deck, our team applied the visual approach to event banners and employee ID badges. Print materials for healthcare projects require meticulous attention to contrast ratios, text legibility at a distance, and color accuracy across many surfaces. Because the green gradient on the screen may differ significantly on the fabric or badge stock. Every asset has the same modular components as the deck, so that the brand reads consistently online and offline.

results.title: Information Architecture Depth

nextgpu.headline: Brand and Web Redesign for DeNet

Its website looked like every other dark, symbol-heavy Web3 platform, so NextGPU asked RZQ for a website redesign, a new logo, and a lighter design direction.

Developers and GPU providers had no clear reason to choose it over any other option. That lack of differentiation put sign-ups and onboarding at risk, so our client asked RZQ for a minimal and credible identity that could build trust without feeling cold or corporate.
nextgpu.solution: RZQ rebuilt the website around a clearer structure and a lighter visual system. The platform is easier to read, navigate, and understand. The logo distills the brand into a minimal, recognizable mark that stays consistent across every digital touchpoint. A new design direction based on accessibility principles and a decentralized technology style without added visual noise.

Its negative space is an arrow for GPU compute that moves between providers and developers. We kept the logo simple rather than using traditional Web3 iconography. nexora.headline: UX/UI Design for a DeFi Analytics Dashboard

nexora.about: Nexora is a DeFi data platform that delivers real-time blockchain insights for quant funds, analysts, and AI-driven trading systems. The team needed a scalable dashboard system that explains dense financial data clearly. Structured visuals should not cut analytical depth.

This process slows down decision-making in a market where every minute affects profitability. Every data point carried the same visual weight, which raised the risk of missing price shifts or protocol anomalies.
nexora.solution: RZQ built a modular dashboard with clear hierarchy, so analysts spot priority signals without scanning entire screens. A structured component library, accent-color system, and scalable UI kit highlight key changes and let Nexora add new data types without rebuilding the interface. We shorten the path from data to decision for faster trade calls and fewer missed signals.

The lime-on-dark hue conveys accuracy and attention. It fits the dashboard's dark UI and maintains identity consistency.

sections.title: RZQ structures high-density data so the right insight reaches first and guides the decision.
